title: Spectrograms, Mel Scale & Audio Features
service: MelKit: a log-mel front end with an on-disk feature cache, deltas, CMVN and layered configs

parts.lesson_anchor: Build It, Steps 4-5 (mel filterbank, log-mel, Whisper's clip + normalize routine); Pitfalls: sample-rate mismatch upstream, dB vs log; code/main.py apply_filterbank (the `if w:` skip)
planted_bugs: hz_to_mel uses math.log with the log10 constant 2595; the error surfaces one call up, in mel_filterbank, as 'mel filter 18 of 40 covers no FFT bins'
log_mel_spectrogram builds the filterbank without passing sr, so mel_filterbank's default of 16000 Hz is used for 8 kHz audio; after the first fix the same error names filter 0 and sr=16000
whisper_log_mel clamps every frame at its own maximum minus 8, although the docstring (and Whisper) clamp at the loudest value in the whole clip
apply_filterbank densifies the sparse filters and multiplies every bin of every filter
parts.timing_assert: 80-mel bank up to 8 kHz on 48 kHz audio (1025 bins), 600 frames under 0.1 s; the dense version takes about 1.3 s, the lesson's `if w:` skip about 0.7 s, the span-only version about 9 ms
parts.overfix_guard: the same 1 kHz tone at 16 kHz with fmax 4000 must land in band 18, which rules out changing the default sample rate to the test's 8000 (band 11); the span-only filterbank must match the dense rows to 1e-12; deleting the empty-filter check leaves the tone in band 7

parts.lesson_anchor: Pitfalls: mel count mismatch and sample-rate mismatch (log the feature shape at both ends)
parts.exactness: float64 feature matrices round-trip bit for bit across a reopen, including subnormals and -1e300; a zero-frame matrix keeps its width; clips one ulp apart hash differently
traps: clip hash without the sample rate
clip hash at reduced precision, down to %.16g
rows checked against the first row, each other or the total count only

parts.lesson_anchor: Exercise 3 (MFCC-13 + delta + delta-delta); Pitfalls: normalization drift (per-utterance normalization)
traps: negative index wraps at the start
zero padding or reflection at the edges
delta-delta from the static features or with the first width
a fixed number of delta orders
CMVN per frame instead of per dimension
parts.integration: Part 1 log-mels -> 120-dimensional static + delta + delta-delta -> CMVN, every dimension mean 0 and variance 1
clarifying_questions: floor on the standard deviation or the variance

parts.lesson_anchor: Pitfalls: normalization drift (training and inference normalize differently); streaming front ends cannot see the whole utterance
parts.wire_format: push() returns a list of normalized frames, possibly empty, and flush() returns the rest; the test concatenates them in order
parts.offline_relation: output frame t equals cmvn(frames[:max(t + 1, warmup)])[t]; the last frame equals offline per-utterance CMVN
parts.timing_assert: 1000 frames of 13 dims pushed one at a time under 0.05 s; recomputing cmvn() over the prefix takes 0.55-0.65 s, Welford about 2 ms
traps: frame normalized before it is counted
warm-up released one frame late or decided by the held count

parts.lesson_anchor: Ship It: skill-feature-extractor (frame/hop, mel count and normalization must match the training config)
traps: base or override aliased into the result, including untouched subtrees
unknown keys accepted, at the top level or below
parts.integration: the fingerprint keys the Part 2 cache through FeatureService: a reordered config hits, a changed n_mels misses

deviations: Part 1: the power spectrum, power_to_db and the log floor are asserted but carry no planted bug, because other Phase 6 packs already plant them (a magnitude for power in 06/16, 20 log10 against power in 06/14, the log of digital silence in 06/11, 06/14 and 06/16); the planted bugs are the mel constant, the filterbank's sample rate, Whisper's clip-level floor and the dense filterbank

Part 1: the timing case covers part of a wide spectrum (80 mels up to 8 kHz on 48 kHz audio); with full-band filters the dense/sparse gap is only about n_mels/2 and cannot give 8x margins on both sides
Part 2: one file per entry under a directory instead of SQLite, so the traps are about precision, shape and keys rather than transactions; the clip hash also covers the sample rate
Part 3: delta widths are per order (windows=[2, 2], like HTK's DELTAWINDOW and ACCWINDOW), which gives Part 5 a list whose order matters
Part 4: a synchronous push/flush API rather than an async generator, plus a timing assertion against recomputing offline CMVN for every frame

Part 5: unknown keys are rejected with their dotted path (a typo like n_mel would otherwise fall back to 80 mels), the fingerprint is checked across processes, and the part ends by keying the Part 2 cache
